modes.name: Flow tracers
modes.summary: A NASA dataset (rain, ozone, carbon monoxide or nitrogen oxides: pick it in the Data menu) with particles following its motion. Press Play: tracers over high values sing, higher values play higher and louder.
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Pick a dataset with the Data menu: NASA real-time precipitation (IMERG), or near-surface ozone, carbon monoxide or nitrogen oxides from NASA's GEOS-CF model. Streams of particles follow the apparent motion of that dataset's pattern (optical flow). Yellow tracers over high values (rain, or above-median gas) sing: a higher value plays higher and louder, west to east pans left to right, the instrument comes from the region. Only the chosen dataset is shown and heard.

modes.name: Precipitation ball
modes.summary: A ball rolls over a terrain raised by NASA IMERG rain, and its motion makes the sound.
modes.author: itay
modes.description: Place a ball on the moving IMERG precipitation video; rain raises a terrain whose slope rolls the ball around, with Web Audio sound following its motion. Keyboard: focus the map, Enter places the ball, arrows move it. From itay's clustering branch.

modes.name: Scanning line
modes.summary: A line sweeps one NASA IMERG rain map west to east and plays it: low notes at the bottom, high at the top, louder where it rains harder.
modes.author: itay
modes.description: A line sweeps across one global IMERG precipitation frame from west to east and plays it as notes on a C major scale, low (C2) at the bottom of the map and high (C5) at the top; the heaviest rain in each band sets that note's volume. From itay's scanning-line-demo branch.

modes.name: Sound lab
modes.summary: The moving NASA rain and snow map as a mixing desk: choose which part of the weather drives pitch, loudness, overtones, instrument, chord and rhythm, with separate rain and snow sounds.
modes.author: balona
modes.description: A mapping playground on the moving NASA IMERG video. Voices follow storms, a scan line, points you drop, or the whole map; for each one the map gives X, Y, speed, spin, color, size and rain or snow, and a mapping table decides which of them drives pitch, amplitude, overtones, instrument (21 synthesized instruments), chord, rhythm, note length, pan and vibrato, with its own shape and range. Rain and snow each have their own key, scale and instruments, and a voice crossfades between them. Strict tuning keeps every note on the scale and on the beat. Storm Watch mode plays the storms tracked in the 7 November snapshots. From balona's sound_demo branch (version 1).

modes.name: Storm picker
modes.summary: Select a storm, preview its rain or snow sound, then press Space to hear its journey through the day.
modes.author: balona
modes.description: A first-frame NASA IMERG storm map. Hover to preview a storm; click to select it; press Space to hear it move through the day. A short tutorial and spoken introduction explain how to listen. Sound controls stay tucked away until needed.

modes.name: Storm watch
modes.summary: Storms in NASA IMERG rain data, tracked over 24 hours. Click a storm or press N to hear it: each region plays its own instrument, bigger storms louder.
modes.author: itay
modes.description: Follow individual storms through 48 half-hourly IMERG frames, tracked offline with computer vision (OpenCV optical flow and watershed). Click a storm, or press N and P on the map, to hear it (hovering only names it): each region plays its own instrument, panned by longitude, and bigger storms are louder (under More, size or latitude can drive pitch or volume instead). Enter follows a storm, and when storms merge and split the whole family stays marked; Page Up and Page Down step through time. The full tracking studio with tuning sliders is linked from the panel. From itay's clustering branch.

modes.name: Tone lab
modes.summary: Hear each region's instrument: click the map. Note, Scale and Chord play the same pitch everywhere, so only the instrument changes.
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Every region of the world has its own instrument. Click or tap a region, or use the arrow keys and Enter, to hear a note, a scale, a chord or its typical phrase, once or on a loop. Recorded and analysed instruments are in the Instrument list.

modes.name: Vortex melodies
modes.summary: Swirls in a NASA dataset (rain, ozone, carbon monoxide or nitrogen oxides: pick it in the Data menu): press Play and every swirl loops its own tune, faster spin plays faster and the dot circles once per tune. Click or press Enter on a swirl to hear it alone; Escape brings back all.
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Pick a dataset with the Data menu: NASA real-time precipitation (IMERG), or near-surface ozone, carbon monoxide or nitrogen oxides from NASA's GEOS-CF model. Swirls in its pattern are found by optical flow and tracked over time. Each swirl loops a short tune: faster spin plays faster, bigger swirls louder; a low hum swells where the pattern converges. Only the chosen dataset is shown and heard.
